source_text:
πλὴν
ἀπόδος αὐτῷ καθ' ἕνωσιν ἀδιάσπαστον τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ, μὴ ἀπογυμνώσῃς αὐτὸν
τοῦ καταπετάσματος· οὕτω γὰρ ἕνα προσκυνήσεις Υἱὸν, ὁμοούσιον μὲν τῷ Πατρὶ
θεϊκῶς, ὁμοούσιον δὲ καὶ ἡμῖν τὸν αὐτὸν ἀνθρωπίνως. τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις
ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν.
βʹ. Ἦν γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ τιμωμένη τε καὶ ἁγιαζομένη· ὅτι
γὰρ τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι, οὔτ' ἂν ἐδεήθη βαπτίσματος, οὔτε μὴν τοῦ Ἁγίου
Πνεύματος μετασχεῖν, μάλιστα μὲν ἀρκέσει πρὸς πληροφορίαν τὸ αὐτὸν εἶναι τοῦ
Πνεύματος χορηγόν.
thought_title: Give back his flesh in inseparable union
orientation: Cyril is addressing Theodore directly, urging him to confess the one Son in an inseparable union of divinity and flesh.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless give back to him according to [an] inseparable union the flesh of him, [do] not strip him of the veil; thus for one you will worship [the] Son, consubstantial indeed with the Father divinely, consubstantial but also with us the same humanly. To those thus to think having chosen will return Christ of the according to himself mystery the knowledge. 2. For was the of man nature the in Christ being honored and being sanctified; for that indeed the at least having come into the being, neither would it have needed of baptism, nor indeed of the Holy Spirit to partake, especially indeed will suffice for full assurance the same to be of the Spirit giver.

choices.term: ἀπόδος αὐτῷ καθ' ἕνωσιν ἀδιάσπαστον τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ
choices.english: give back to him in an inseparable union his flesh
choices.why: Keeps the imperative force and the dative of advantage; 'give back' renders ἀποδίδωμι as a return of what is owed, matching the argument that the flesh belongs to the Word.
rejected: restore to him his flesh in an inseparable union
assign to him his flesh according to an inseparable union

choices.english: do not strip him of the veil
choices.why: The glossary requires 'veil' for καταπέτασμα; the verb ἀπογυμνόω means to strip bare, and the genitive of separation is preserved.
rejected: do not denude him of the curtain
do not uncover him from the veil

choices.term: τοῖς οὕτω φρονεῖν ᾑρημένοις ἀναστρέψει Χριστὸς τοῦ καθ' ἑαυτὸν μυστηρίου τὴν γνῶσιν
choices.english: To those who have chosen to think thus Christ will turn back the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself
choices.why: ἀναστρέφω here means to turn back or reveal; the perfect participle ᾑρημένοις is rendered as 'who have chosen'; 'concerning himself' renders καθ' ἑαυτὸν.
rejected: Christ will return the knowledge of the mystery about himself to those who have chosen to think thus
Christ will overturn the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself for those who have chosen to think thus

choices.term: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι
choices.english: as to what pertains to being
choices.why: The phrase τό γε ἧκον εἰς τὸ εἶναι is an idiom meaning 'as far as concerns existence'; the rendering keeps the limiting force of γε.
rejected: as far as coming into being is concerned

choices.english: most of all it will suffice for full assurance
choices.why: ἀρκέσει is future indicative; πληροφορία is rendered 'full assurance' per the glossary sense of certainty; μάλιστα μέν is kept as 'most of all'.
rejected: especially it will be enough for conviction
above all it will suffice for certainty

pass_b_english: But give back to him his flesh in an inseparable union, and do not strip him of the veil. For in this way you will worship one Son, consubstantial with the Father divinely, and the same one consubstantial with us humanly. To those who have chosen to think thus, Christ will reveal the knowledge of the mystery concerning himself.

For the nature of humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified. As to what pertains to being, he would not have needed baptism, nor to share in the Holy Spirit. Most of all it will suffice for full assurance that he himself is the giver of the Spirit.

problems.quote: the nature of the human being in Christ
problems.source_quote: ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ
problems.why: ἀνθρώπου is genitive 'of the human/humanity', not 'human being'; makes Christ sound like a container.
problems.fix: For the nature of humanity in Christ was being honored and sanctified.

edits.old: the nature of the human being in Christ
edits.new: the nature of humanity in Christ

fixed: Changed 'the nature of the human being in Christ' to 'the nature of humanity in Christ' because the source has ἀνθρώπου (genitive of 'humanity/human'), not 'human being'.

last_rejected.quote: Most of all it will suffice for full assurance
last_rejected.why: "Most of all" misreads μάλιστα μέν, which means "above all" or "especially" as a rhetorical intensifier, not a comparative ranking; the point is supreme sufficiency, not relative sufficiency among options.
last_rejected.fix: Above all, it will suffice for full assurance
last_rejected.ruling: μάλιστα commonly means 'especially' or 'above all'; 'most of all' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: The Greek uses an aorist optative with ἄν (potential unreal), not a counterfactual conditional; the English "would not have needed" wrongly implies a contrary-to-fact scenario rather than a simple potentiality ("he would not need").
last_rejected.ruling: οὔτ' ἂν ἐδεήθη with ἄν + aorist is potential; 'would not have needed' is standard English rendering, not a real error.
